title: Pricing methods
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers pricing methods; the closest ones cover profit and competitors in general, not how a business sets its prices.

draft.title: Pricing methods
card: the business works out the cost of making or buying one unit, then adds a markup for profit. A unit that costs $20 with a 50% markup sells for $30.
the business sets a price by what customers are willing to pay, which depends on demand. It may charge more when demand is strong and less when it is weak.
the business sets its price by looking at what competitors charge. It may match them, or price slightly above or below.
The methods look at different things: the business's own costs, customers, or rivals. Cost-based pricing starts from cost, not from what the market will pay.
draft.remember: Each method starts from a different place: cost, customers or competitors.

a.q: Which business is using cost-based pricing?
opts: It adds 40% to the cost of each unit it makes
It sets prices after checking what rivals charge
It raises prices when customers rush to buy
It lowers prices when fewer customers are buying
a.why: Adding a fixed markup to the unit cost is cost-based pricing. Checking rivals is competition-based, and changing prices as demand rises or falls is market-based.
a.clue: Which one starts from what the product costs the business?

b.q: Priya sells phone cases in Parramatta. A new stall opens nearby and sells similar cases for $15. She drops her price from $18 to $15 to match it. Which method is she using?
b.why: Priya is setting her price by what a rival charges, so this is competition-based pricing. It is not market-based, because she is not responding to changes in customer demand. Her costs did not change either, so it is not cost-based.
b.clue: What caused her to change the price: her costs, her customers or a rival?

a.best: It adds 40% to the cost of each unit it makes
